pageTitle: Calculate Your University of Minnesota GPA

officialLinks.label: Grading scale; GPA formula; symbols; repeats
Transcript grading history and Law exception

helpIntro: University of Minnesota Twin Cities uses a 4.000 GPA scale for standard A-F courses. Enter semester credits and final grades to estimate your current or projected GPA.
helpNote: S/N grades and transcript symbols are excluded from GPA. For eligible undergraduate repeats, the most recent enrollment replaces the earlier attempt in GPA; graduate and Law records use different rules.
helpExample: A 3-credit A earns 12 grade points; a 3-credit B+ earns 9.999. Together, 21.999 ÷ 6 = 3.667.

gradeExplanations.F: F earns 0 grade points; course credits count in GPA.
gradeExplanations.S: S is excluded from GPA; degree credit may count if allowed.
gradeExplanations.N: N is excluded from GPA and earns no degree credit.
gradeExplanations.I: Incomplete is excluded until resolved; undergraduate I may lapse to F or N under policy.
gradeExplanations.X: Continuation-course symbol; excluded until replaced by a final grade.
gradeExplanations.K: Course-in-progress symbol; excluded until replaced by a final grade.
gradeExplanations.NR: No grade reported; carries no GPA points.

specialTypes.name: U of M course, standard A-F/S-N grading
specialTypes.note: Use for standard U of M coursework. S/N and transcript symbols are excluded by grade rule.

specialTypes.name: External transfer course
specialTypes.note: Accepted external transfer credits can affect degree/SAP credit measures but do not enter the U of M GPA.

specialTypes.name: Twin Cities Law School course
specialTypes.note: Law allows A+ 4.333 and excludes D+; use the Law record rather than this undergraduate profile.

repeatPolicy.note: For an eligible undergraduate repeat, only the most recent enrollment counts in GPA, even if the new grade is lower. An N does not replace a prior F; third attempts and repeatable-for-credit courses need review.
